summary: EPOS (development-related postgraduate courses) is a DAAD scholarship programme, funded by the German development ministry, for graduates from developing and newly industrialised countries with at least two years of professional experience. It gives individual scholarships for selected development-related master's courses at German universities and, in exceptional cases, doctoral study. You apply directly to the course (up to three), and a selection committee proposes candidates to the DAAD. The 2027/2028 intake list names about 26 courses, with deadlines set by each course.
eligibility_notes:
You must be a graduate from any discipline from one of the developing or newly industrialised countries on the DAAD country list (based on the OECD DAC list of developing countries), with at least two years of related professional experience after your first degree at the time of application.

The typical holder works for a public authority or a state or private company in a developing country, on development policy projects in technology, economics or social areas. You need a bachelor's degree (normally four years) in a related subject, completed with far above-average results (upper third). The degree should normally be no more than six years old. There is no age limit. If your country has only three-year bachelor's degrees, ask the university whether you can apply.

Applicants who have been in Germany for more than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered. If you already hold a master's degree and apply for another master's course, you must argue well why you should be funded for a second one.

You do not need to be admitted to the master's course before you apply for the scholarship. If the deadline of a course has passed you cannot apply to it.

Language: for courses taught in German, you need a B1 certificate at application, and DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 must be passed before the studies start (a preparatory six-month German course in Germany is included). The page says it is not possible to pass these tests without at least B1 beforehand. For English-taught courses, proof follows each course's own rules; IELTS or TOEFL is named in the document list and the institutional TOEFL is not accepted. Ask the course whether an institutional score or an unofficial copy is acceptable.

Candidates must also show development-related motivation and be expected to take on social responsibility and support change in their personal and professional environment after the studies. Each university course has its own selection criteria in addition to the DAAD's. The announcement of scholarships depends on funds from the German development ministry (BMZ).
age_experience_notes: No age limit. At least two years of relevant professional experience after the first degree are needed at the time of application, shown by employer certificates (ideally with a re-employment guarantee). The first degree should normally be no more than six years old.
funding_summary: Funding lasts 12 to 42 months depending on the course. Graduates receive EUR 992 per month and doctoral candidates EUR 1,300 per month (EUR 1,400 from February 2026), plus contributions toward health, accident and personal liability insurance and a travel allowance unless another source pays for travel. Under certain circumstances there is also a monthly rent subsidy and a monthly allowance for accompanying family members. Tuition fees are not paid by the student, but registration or enrolment fees may be due. For German-taught courses a preparatory six-month German course in Germany is included.
programmes_note: Funding is only for the courses on the DAAD list for the 2027/2028 intake, for their full length; it is not available for a master's you have already started or been admitted to if it is not on the list. The list groups courses under economic sciences, business administration and political economics; engineering and related sciences; regional and urban planning; agricultural and forest sciences; natural and environmental sciences; medicine and public health; and social sciences. Doctoral funding is possible only in exceptional cases.
institutions_note: Courses are at German universities, some with partner institutions abroad: Göttingen, Leipzig, Bochum, Bonn (with the United Nations University), TU Dresden, Flensburg, Oldenburg, HfT Stuttgart, Bauhaus-Universität Weimar, TU Berlin, Stuttgart with Ain Shams University, Hohenheim, Bremen, TU Darmstadt, Freiburg, Greifswald, TH Köln (also with the German Jordanian University and Universidad de San Luis Potosi), Charité Berlin with FU Berlin and HU Berlin, Heidelberg, and PH Ludwigsburg with Helwan University Cairo. You choose the course; you may apply to up to three.

requirements.text: Completed and signed checklist (ticked off and signed by hand).
Completed EPOS (DAAD) application form, typed or clearly readable. If you apply to more than one course, list them in priority order in section 7 and do not change the order.
CV in reverse chronological order in Europass format, without unexplained gaps, with exact information on studies and practical experience and the date of issue.

One letter of motivation of at most two pages with the date, covering academic, professional and personal reasons. For more than one course (maximum three) the same letter goes to every course and must explain the choice and ranking of courses.
Letter of recommendation from your current employer, on official letterhead with signature and official stamp, of current date, not in a sealed envelope.

Certificate(s) of employment from your employer(s) showing at least two years of relevant work experience after the bachelor's degree up to the time of application; from the current employer ideally with a guarantee of re-employment after you return home. On headed paper with an original or code-certified digital signature, date and stamp.
Recent proof of language skills: English (IELTS or TOEFL; institutional TOEFL not accepted) or as the course requires; German for German-taught courses (certificate no older than one year, level B1).
requirements.conditional_rule: German proof only for courses taught in German

requirements.text: Copies of higher education degree certificates, clearly legible; certified translation if not in German or English. Check whether the university wants certified copies.
Copy of the full set of transcripts, with an explanation of the grading system if it is not part of the transcript.
APS certificate (from the Akademische Prüfstelle of the German Embassy).
requirements.conditional_rule: applicants from the People's Republic of China only

requirements.text: Any additional documents the course itself asks for; see the course website. Applications must be in English or German and complete.

application_steps.title: Choose up to three courses on the 2027/2028 list
application_steps.detail: Only courses on the DAAD list for the 2027/2028 intake are funded. Check each course's own entry rules, language needs and deadline on its website; a deadline that has passed cannot be reopened. Development Management has an intake only every two years, with the next in 2028.

application_steps.title: Prepare the documents in the required order
application_steps.detail: Checklist signed by hand, EPOS application form, Europass CV, one letter of motivation (two pages at most), employer recommendation, employment certificates for at least two years, language proof, degree certificates, transcripts and, for China, an APS certificate. The same letter of motivation must go to every course and explain the ranking if you apply to more than one.

application_steps.title: Send the application directly to each course
application_steps.detail: Apply to the course itself, not the DAAD, in English or German, following the course's own procedure (some use an online form, and the course says whether email is allowed). Anything sent to the DAAD is not forwarded, and incomplete applications cannot be considered. You do not need to be admitted before applying for the scholarship.

application_steps.title: Course selection committee proposes candidates
application_steps.detail: A selection committee suggests potential candidates for a DAAD scholarship. The DAAD criteria are upper-third results, at least two years of related experience, development-related motivation and a convincing letter; each course adds its own criteria. Shortlisted candidates have a telephone interview with university staff, which the applicant must take alone.

application_steps.title: Upload full application to the DAAD portal when asked
application_steps.detail: Suggested candidates are contacted by the DAAD and asked to upload their complete application to the DAAD portal as PDF files, so keep a copy of every document. The selection is then finalised and suggested candidates are informed. The DAAD gives no status information; the course informs you, and most selection is finished by March.

application_steps.title: Prepare for studies in Germany
application_steps.detail: For German-taught courses you need to pass DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 before the course starts, after the included six-month German course; passing the test is a formal condition for enrolment. All holders pay no tuition fees but may owe registration or enrolment fees. Funding runs for the course length, 12 to 42 months.

application_steps.title: Family and return arrangements
application_steps.detail: Accompanying family members may get a monthly allowance and a rent subsidy may be paid in some circumstances. Employers are asked to certify that they will re-employ you on return, if possible. The pages read set no other return duty or reporting duty.

The list of courses is a table whose text extract mixes columns, so per-course language, degree and duration were confirmed only where the rows were unambiguous (Hydro Science and Engineering, the two International Health courses, INEMA); other courses carry only the field group and institution. The institution of 'Global Health' and the exact pairing for 'Development Cooperation' could not be read from the extract.
Course websites were not opened, so course-specific entry rules, deadlines and documents are not included.
